body: I purchased a 12-month subscription to TomTom GO Navigation via their official website, expecting full access to navigation features, including truck routing. After purchasing, I used the truck navigation without issues, but later, TomTom suddenly removed access and demanded an additional €80 for truck navigation, despite their own advertising and UI indicating it was part of my subscription. Customer support has been completely unhelpful and refuses to escalate the case. They repeatedly send copy-paste responses, ignoring clear evidence that their advertising was misleading. Instead of addressing the issue, they insist I should have known Truck Navigation was separate—despite no clear disclaimer on their website. 🚨 TomTom is misleading customers by falsely advertising truck navigation features as part of their GO Navigation subscription and then retroactively restricting access. If you are a truck driver, stay away from this app unless you want to be scammed into paying twice. Their support team will ignore you and refuse to acknowledge their own misleading marketing. Now, they even replied to my review here, claiming they “want to hear more about my issue.” I followed their instructions, sent an email, and… nothing. No response. No resolution. Just silence. title: Never fix the actual problems, just rearrange things.
body: When I first got this app years ago there were many options. You could choose map colors, change the guidance icon from an arrow to various cars with different colors, plan a route with several stops and the stops would be numbered so you could tell where it was routing you first, second, and so on. It was the best GPS app. You paid one standard fee for North America and that was it. There wasn’t traffic updates but, it was awesome. Now after several updates, they changed the colors and you don’t have ANY option to change any colors. There is no option to change your guidance icon, if you plan a route with several stops, they are no longer numbered so you have no idea where it’s sending you first so you have to go into the route options and choose “reorder route” every time you plan one and route it yourself. Now there is a subscription model and, I get it, you make more money getting a subscription than you do if I buy the app once. You do get traffic updates now but there are so many more bugs since you “improved” the app with updates. Addresses change on you after they are entered if there are more than one stop. I have sent several emails to TomTom about this and have even sent in a video showing them the issues. Then they update the app and give you the new feature of not having your music level lowered during instructions. 🤦🏻‍♂️ Yeah, THAT has been a real problem. How about giving us some of those options back. I’d love to be able to change the color of my planed route, change the guidance icon or at least it’s color. When it’s the same at the route color, it blends in. I’d imagine people that are colorblind would be very appreciative to be able to have some contrast between route and icon. If you don’t want people to use your app and only want people to buy your stand alone GPS products, then remove your app from the App Store and just make standalone product. If you keep your app in the App Store, the least you can do is fix the bugs and give us some real options instead of music volume. UPDATE: It is now August 12th, 2024 and none of the items mentioned above have been addressed. I have sent several emails to TomTom showing addresses changing after entered and they can’t fix this simple problem. Today I entered an address as 6721 Sylvan rd and the app changed it to 6700 sylvan rd. Depending on how houses are spaced, this could be half a mile down the road.

title: Want to Support TT but Feel Cheated
body: The Tom Tom NAV app was the most money that I had ever spent on a single app, but when I did so I felt it was worth the money because I believed in a paid app that protected my privacy instead of going with something free like google maps or Waze. The app worked beautifully and I purchased additional maps to use when traveling internationally. All that ended a few years ago when they decided to abandon the original app, and forced everyone to move over to a completely new app that had a subscription model. They sent emails and messages saying we would get access for a specified period of time. If I had purchased a hardware Tom Tom nav device it would still work, but because I purchased the iPhone app, they could simply pull the plug and I was out of luck. Not only that but when I tried to use the new app it was missing 80-90 of the original features. Besides the features that were now missing, the new app was simply unusable, and the reviews bear testimony to that. 99% of the time when I tried to load the app, it wouldn’t even start up. So while the subscription was free for the people who had previously spent a lot of money for the original app, the new app was useless. Within the last year, they finally added back most of the features that was present in the original app, and things were starting to look promising. The new problem ow was that the subscription period that they had given to the people who owned the original app had expired. To summarize, loyal Tom Tom users spent hundreds of dollars to buy a navigation app when there were plenty of free options available. title: I'm done

I still have ~3 months left on the free nav they gave owners of the old app but there are so many better options there's no point riding it out any longer. Address and point of interest searching is still needlessly complicated (why are they even separate?) and the ui is still slow and awkward enough that I miss turns regularly. This is truly an app stuck in the dark ages of dedicated hardware nav and I'm moving on. Old review follows: The new graphics engine is nice. That's the only positive thing I can say about this. The new subscription model is a terrible idea. With the old app I could pay once and use the maps and routing as much as I wanted and pay for traffic on the occasions when I wanted it. The traffic routing is so ineffective as to be pointless. The maps, directions, and coordinates don't match up. The directions frequently end a block or more away from my actual destination. In a dense city, that makes them worthless. I have to switch to my built-in maps app to get the last few blocks. The "near me" search area is always too small. If I want to search anywhere in my own city, I have to enter the city name first, which is a huge pain. Finally, it constantly directs me to do dangerous or illegal things. Things like illegal turns and trying to cross 3 lanes of traffic and a median to make a left turn coming off the interstate. Naturally, tomtom has been unresponsive to reports about their broken maps and dangerous directions. I'm done with these guys. It's been a good run but it's obvious that quality has tanked and won't be improving any time soon.

title: Worst ever
body: The good thing is that it’s graphically very slick and not silly like other GPS apps. But the bad is the navigation itself. Particularly over highways. It doesn’t announce highway names or numbers most of the time. You have to look at the screen to get the exact direction. Also, while on a highway and being directed to exit, it once it told me to exit at a weird street name when the exit is actually called something else (it said “exit 19, Warlow st” when the exit is actually some other name, and boulevard, not street. ). Sometimes it names the highway. Sometimes it just says the highway number (“i123”) rather than the name. Sometimes (most times) it just says “freeway”, not the highway name OR number. It never ever says exactly what’s on the actual road signs. There is no reconciliation between what signs you see on the road and what you hear from the GPS. Very disorienting. I’ve been using this app to navigate me to places I already know how to get to, just to test it out. If I didn’t already know where I was going, this app would confuse me and get me lost. (UPDATE: The app has since disoriented me and gotten me lost while going to a place That I didn’t know how to get to on my own, since I first wrote this review ) The navigation is really bad. Also while the app is visually slick it’s confusing to interface with during a trip. Oh and also there are no voice alerts when it alerts you of a traffic camera or anything else. Just an audible blip. You have to look at the screen to see what it’s alerting you to, because there’s no voice alert. And you have to look at the screen to see what highway to take also. It’s like the developer doesn’t realize drivers need to watch the road and not have to look at their GPS screen. I can’t believe this was made by TomTom. It seems like it was made by an amateur GPS company rather than by an old staple like TomTom. This app looks beautiful but functions very badly.

title: Feels a decade old
body: I was hoping to find an alternative to the standard map apps, as I won’t use Google and Apple Maps has become progressively less usable (just try to navigate pins and saved places across platforms!), so I was willing to pay a well-known third party to try their navigation in CarPlay. Unfortunately this isn’t it. The maps seem ok, and the interface has some interesting elements - like a progress bar to your destination with distance to gas stations (although how often do you need that to be a permanent map element?) - but the voicing for turn by turn is atrocious compared to Siri and the Google voice. The “computer” voices that can announce street names talk in a stilted manner circa 2010 and even mispronounce simple common street names like “Whatever Ave” (“Whatever ayve”). There’s also no mention of live traffic rerouting, though I guess it’s possible it exists, and no browser or desktop-based companion. What I really want is simply to be able to create my own routes like you’ve been able to do forever using drag and drop in Google Maps desktop, then sync those specific routes to your phone. Oh well, back to Apple Maps I go, and hope that it can eventually clean up the pinned locations and sync the desktop and mobile apps properly. And, maybe, someday allow me to just make my own routes without clunky waypoints.

title: Not the best.
body: I’m my opinion, this navigation app needs some work. Pros: I really do enjoy the way the lanes get marked out and it highlights which one you should be in! Navigation is good haven’t had many problems finding most basic restaurants or shops. I have not used it at all but I know the offline maps would be very useful!! I like the way it places gas stations on your route so you can fill up along the way and don’t have to go to side menus to add a gas station to my route. As odd as it may sound, I really love the way the narrators/voices navigators have really fun personalities!! A lot of apps and maps like Google and Waze have really bland and straight forward navigation which is to be expected but it doesn’t sound natural. Which is why I enjoy Apples voice navigation. Cons: Well I’ll just start with… Cost, not that it’s too expensive but the fact that it cost anything while being a pretty bland app with not too many features to pay for. Not so common places are not easy to find. You have to know the correct address and you have to find it and maybe even look it up while I can easily look it up on Google and even get directions right away. Design, the design of the app is kinda complicated at first and can be ugly when compared to Google and Apple which have trees and certain buildings plotted around to better identify your location. This may sound odd seeing as how I raved about the voice narrators in my cons but they are way too active. They will repeat things over and over again all the time. Last minute turns, I’ve had a lot of times where it’s not giving me clear instructions so I end up being confused on my exit or have to make last minute decisions, for it advertising it as one of its many features, it fails in that aspect. I have many more but this list is getting long. My TLDR: If you drive a lot and need a second opinion navigating app or want to try it out… use TomTom. If you just need a basic navigation app for finding a meet up with your friends or family… just use Apple or Google.

title: No Sound!
body: Just installed, signed up for the trial. Really wanted to use this as I got rid of waze. Didn't want to use Google. Was working great for about an hour then no sound. body: I had high hopes given that the app is a pay one and Tomtom has been around for a long time but it was disappointing. When navigating, the vehicle location shown in the app lags the voice by some distance and it got the name wrong on a major street into the subdivision where I live. The worst problem is that the app continually momentarily freezes and then jumps ahead to catch up. After watching that on a thirty mile driving trip it very quickly became really annoying. title: Poor CarPlay integration
body: My wife has a vehicle with Tom Tom native navigation, and it works really well, even with the vehicles voice system. While I have Apple Maps, Google Maps and Waze, I figured I’d download this on my iPhone, and use it via CarPlay I’m my Jeep. Unfortunately, there is no support for Siri voice input, and also no voice input via the screen. For me that’s a deal breaker. The one thing this app does well, is locating you on the Highway vs the access roads. Nice, but not so much better that I’d pay for this vs using Waze. If you don’t need to navigate out of cell service range, I’d suggest passing on this app. I’ll be deleting it.

Off the bat, I was very disappointed that you have to pay for traffic info, etc. where that is free on other map apps. Major interstates are instead stated as US highways. No traffic camera notifications like I get on Waze. No mic search or address entry, need to use the phone instead of the screen. While this is visually nice map and the developers did a nice job so far, I don’t feel that the price is worth it compared with the other alternatives that are out there for free.

title: Offline Mode Concern during Hurricane
body: I recently purchased a family subscription, one of the main reasons for the decision was offline maps downloaded so I could navigate if there was no cellular service. I have been having issues with the widget not working saying something to the effect of check my subscription, which had already been processed. I deleted the app and reinstalled all my maps again still same issue. I live in central/south Florida’s and we recently had hurricane Ian wreck everything around us. I had no cellular service, could not even get a simple SMS text through. We had to check on a friend of the family and wasn’t sure about how to get there so I started my TomTom app and nothing. It kept telling me it could not verify my subscription. When I needed it the most for truly offline it failed. I’m writing this review to the developers, please look into this issue. title: Needs Work
body: I really wanted to give this app a top rating but I can’t. Unlike prior versions, the current version of this app when used with Apple CarPlay is way too unstable. It often freezes and requires a restart while driving which is annoying and sometimes very difficult to do safely. No other CarPlay navigation app I have ever used has frozen even once. Also, a strength of this app had been its ability to guide to an alternate route when traffic warrants. Several versions ago they got rid of this and replaced it with a green line on the screen showing a faster route but without the audio guidance. This requires the driver to study the screen, usually in heavy traffic, to figure out the alternative and follow it, a task that is often difficult and dangerous while driving, making this feature useless. There is a lot to like in this app but tomtom has a lot of work to do to get it to top tier. Team tomtom I have already tried deleting and reinstalling with phone reset. I am using an iPhone 7 with iOS 14.7.1. What is the timetable for getting this fixed? Also, what about my second point regarding rerouting enroute due to traffic? Is there any intention and timeframe to fix this?

title: Maps per state, seriously?
body: I’ve been a TomTom user for over 15 years and have always been a strong supporter of what I believed was their technological superiority to all others especially new comers like Waze. I have enjoyed many times the fact that the maps were stored in my phone, allowing me to drive in all safety even when reception gets sketchy, which basically no other iPhone competitors can provide. I’ve even been supportive of their business model pivot when they decided to switch to subscription based, knowing fully all the advantages of having permanent traffic updates and worldwide maps all bundled together. I found their offer of 3 years of subscription very fair in compensation for the app I had paid $100 a few years ago, being aware of the benefits of such system. I however must say that I was baffled by this update that included Maps per State. Living in NY, where you very often cross state line unknowingly, this makes absolutely zero sense. I wanted to go to Boston, so I downloaded NY and MA maps, and was surprised by the travel time calculated by the app - only to realize I had to download also CT for the app to be able to calculate a route through that state instead of around !! No prompt, no suggestion, no nothing. Had I not known roughly the distance between the 2 cities I would have followed blindly the direction and would have followed a - literally - dumb route. I then tested a few situations to make sure it was not me being stupid. If you want to go to Philadelphia, you have to download first the map of PA before you can even start searching for the city - without the map, the app just tells you that Philadelphia does not exist. If you’re visiting friends in Kansas City, I hope for you they’re not in MO - otherwise you’ll be in trouble picking up your rental at the airport that’s in KS ! And I’m not even talking about foreigners using the app exactly because the promise is maps are preloaded and don’t need a local phone plan - unless you have to cross a state line! This is beyond absurd, and I’m finding myself in the most stupid situation where I have to establish my route beforehand using a third party app and then make sure all states are downloaded before I can start pre setting my route in Go. I can no longer trust the app to find the best route - if the app can find a route at all, that is. ***EDIT***Response to developers response I’m not sure exactly what you expect from me regarding that support link you put in your response. If you want me to restate what I stated above I’m sure you can copy and paste my comment in your ticket software. Besides, I litteraly can’t get past the faq section of that page to get to the message section. Not only am I unsure on where to click as your website is designed to make sure people read all the faq before they talk to you, but also I’m violently prompted at every click by an extremely annoying pop in that demands my feedback. On mobile, I can’t even go past it and find myself stuck in the middle of my navigation. It looks like it’s the same guy who designed your website that designed the new version of the app ...

title: Downloaded for use with CarPlay

Apple Maps is great, but when you are in a low signal area, it can’t re-route you should you need to go off-route. Two issues with TomTom app made it a no-go for use with CarPlay: 1. the app, while using CarPlay, had trouble locking onto GPS and could not give me proper routing instructions; 2. the displayed map was a horrible and paired with the GPS issue made the app not worth keeping. I tried using it on two occasions but I gave up and switched back Apple Maps. By the way, I tried Sygic’s app for CarPlay and it was not much better. title: Not worth It when there are better options
body: I really wanted to like this app, because my entire family lives in the Netherlands, and when I see their TomYoms in use, I’m always impressed by the interface while navigating. I like that the navigational view looks like it’s from the drivers perspective, rather than overhead. However, after using Waze for eight years, I find I really can’t get excited about this app. Within the first mile I drove with it, it made two navigational errors (the most serious of which was telling me to make an illegal U-turn so that I could get on the freeway, rather than turn right and use the onramp which DID appear on the map). Also, because it seems this app does not learn from use like Waze does, I can’t simply tap this error location to alert the developers to correct this error, or even use a map editing function online. Also, when using this with CarPlay, during turn-by-turn directions, it does not pause whatever I am listening to through my phone, as does Waze. So if I have an audiobook playing while driving and navigating, I have to keep backing up so that I don’t miss parts of the story. So far, there’s just not enough to like about this app to make it worth spending subscription money, especially when I can basically ignore the ads in Waze and use that for free, while it’s also a better app for my needs.

Let’s start: - The map took too long to download, and was only one. - Horrible color choice and no option to change it. - Map it’s NOT updated, doesn’t have my address making impossible to set my house, and no option to just set a location on the map, as every app does. I couldn’t find any market that exists for years in my city. - Why choose between Address, POI or contact option? The app should search globally for the text. This just make this app just not usable. Come on guys, you used to be the best, and I hope you could again, but you the community, you need better visual, better text search, overall better usability, TomTom right now is way behind. I sincerely wish your company a good comeback. If you don’t have a guy over there to lead the way call me, I’ll work there just to help you guys to get your place again in gps. All the best, but I’m not subscribing, for now.

title: Needs a Little More
body: For the most part, the app works well; however, while testing it, the app has taken me to two bridges that were lower than my vehicle setting of 12’08”. Also, when your destination is on a main road, it fails to tell you which side it is on; this is very helpful information when driving a large rig as you want to know what lane you need to be in and where you’re going to be turning. It’s also a bit sketchy on exits, sometimes it tells you the exit number, sometimes it doesn’t. One 190 in Buffalo it told me to take exit 50… there’s exit 50A and 50B. Basically, this app is a game of “maybe, maybe not”. Maybe you’ll hit a bridge, maybe you won’t. Maybe you have to turn left, maybe right. Just make sure you leave yourself extra time for wrong turns and evasive maneuvers if you want to use it. And don’t EVER trust the height limitations.

title: Works but be careful to check map coverage.
body: TL;DR: Bought a subscription to use on a holiday drive and then found out that maps for the country I want (China) is not included. Applied for a refund and Apple declined to give it to me. I now have a subscription that I can’t use. Dinged one star for that. I live in Australia and I was planning a driving holiday into the countryside where there was poor mobile phone coverage, hence no Waze. I downloaded TomTom because of the option for offline maps. I had two TomTom ONE GPS units from many years ago and I was optimistic that it would not disappoint. After two weeks of use, I found the TomTom app navigation to be acceptable, no better and no worse than other mapping applications. Three things that bugged me. 1. The startup time for the app is too slow compared to the other navigation apps. I timed it at between 10 to 15 seconds which is not long but other apps pop up immediately so that’s they standard I apply. 2. The interface is not as optimised as other navigation apps. The layout of the options feels very unoptimsed for iphone screens; it’s like someone took the TomTom GPS device interface and slapped it on an app. There are too many steps for some very frequent tasks. For example it take way too many taps and screens to select the address of a contact person. 3. Some of the navigation suggestions are plain weird and sometimes dangerous, like trying to get me to cut across three lanes of traffic to take a right turn. (We drive on the left here.) Overall an adequate app for navigation that is worth the subscription to get offline maps and save on roaming charges BUT check that the country you want is covered otherwise you’ll waste your money like I did. /sam

Then a first problem: it was correctly directing me to jump on the freeway, but kept calling it with the “dedicated” name (M. L. King Jr freeway) which is NOWHERE in any sign, instead than it’s official designation that is in every sign for miles around (I-580/Ù.S. 395 North). If I was in an unknown area I would have been very uncertain. Getting to Costco it wanted me to exit at the wrong exit and drive into local roads instead than the right exit that is just in front of Costco, and I think the reason is that it did not recognize the parking lot entry on the freeway side. In fact, when I was leaving it kept insisting I go the other side, only changing when I was fifty yards from the intersection. I choose a different route to return, and even if it was correct in the general direction it had a strange go around half way through. When I got to the suggested turn it was showing I was 13minutes and 6.9 miles from arrival. I kept going the right way and it immediately recalculate to 13 minutes and 5.1 miles. Difficult to understand why I would have had to drive 1.8 more miles than necessary… All of that said, I will keep an eye on it in the next few days but it seems unlikely I will keep it. Pity, the app is nice, several interesting features and very modern graphic… :-(

body: I wanted a navigation app to use when traveling in both my car and RV, one that would work with Apple CarPlay so I could use it on the vehicle information system and did not require internet access for maps because I am frequently in rural areas with little cell coverage. GO Navigation seemed to fit the bill, so I downloaded it and began to use it. In terms of navigation usage the app is great, and I particularly like the weekly map updates since the other navigation systems with on-board maps I used only had 4 month updates. However the main issue for me is that the app does not seem to allow the saving of Routes. Saving Favorites is easy, but if you want to travel a specific way to avoid specific areas and modify the recommended way by adding way-points you do not seem able to save that modified route, and that is a serious issue because it means that every time you need to take a specific route you have to again manually modify it. Interestingly this functionality does exist in the Android version of this app, but not in the iPhone version. Support requests have not been any help. Most responses told me to reinstall the app or to open dialog screens that do not exist on the iOS version of the app. After repeated requests support finally told me that the functionality is missing from the iPhone version . If I could save routes this would be a 5 star review. Without it I can only give 3 stars.

title: Great promise, but not yet worth paying for.
body: I’m impressed to see consistent developer responses to reviews here, so I’m posting this in hopes of getting feedback through to the TomTom product development team. I’m a long time TomTom user, in most recent years with a 620. But it has been an exercise is regular frustration, between flaky smartphone and cloud account connectivity, often slow response to input/commands, not infrequent bugginess, and poor search/POI database/voice control. With the advent of CarPlay (and perhaps even without it), it’s enough to lead one to give up on it and just use Waze/Google maps/whatever. But there’s one key thing that all the other apps fail to do, and that’s to provide simple capability to switch between 2D and 3D views. Don’t ask me why, but it’s missing. And that’s enough for me to be willing to pay for an app with a better UI that supports such. $12.99/year doesn’t seem unreasonable to me. But I find that TomTom GO still has serious shortcomings (which are sometimes rather perplexing). Fix these, and I think you will have a winner. Absent them, I probably can’t justify paying for a subscription once my free trial ends. Roughly in order from most critical must haves, to least critical nice-to-haves: 1. Voice support!!! How can you not have this? Probably the biggest advantage Google maps and the like have is that you can speak a point of interest (or address), and it pulls it right up. Having to type it in doesn’t work for navigating on the fly—which has got to be the primary use case! (And it seems you have even managed to break the voice recognition built into the keyboard, when accessed from the phone! So there's no workaround there.) 2. Fix your POI database I recently tried to pull up directions to a nearby Bloomingdale’s. Pulled up every store except the one closest to me. The store has been there for decades. Fix your database! 3. Enlarge button sizes on CarPlay view (or just the acceptable touch zones, even if not the visible button size) Not everybody has a huge display. Even with a large display, the touch zones are probably too small. (Remember, people are doing this while driving!) It typically takes me multiple tries to successfully select a button (saying a + or - for zoom control) that I’m targeting (and each miss means you have to do an extra press to exit back to normal mode, in order to try again). The usability needs work, and this really isn’t hard to get right. 4. Preserve the zoom level that was last set If I set a zoom level, it probably means that’s the zoom level I’m interested in seeing. Why would you automatically reset it back to whatever zoom is your default? (The 620 mostly gets this right.) You’re just constantly forcing me to reset the zoom level to what I want it to be, every time I launch the app. 5. Preserve zoom level through route updates On a related note, just because you made an adjustment to the route, doesn’t mean I want you to reset the zoom level from where I had it set, to your new route default of showing the entire route. Again, you’re just forcing me to do work—while driving—to reset what I had already set. very user unfriendly. 6. Enlarge exit info, and change color (black on yellow is not optimal contrast) Small, black (or is it dark green) letters on a yellow background for exit numbers may look cool, but it’s not easy to read. I ought to be able to read the exit number with a quick glance. This color scheme may be ok with larger type, but this is certainly broken on my small screen CarPlay unit. It needs to be fixed. 7. Don’t block CarPlay operation just because you updated the app!!! I recently started out driving, and when the app launched, I discovered it required action on the phone. Turns out, it has updated recently, and wanted to give me a tour of new features. Seriously? You’re going to block the app from functioning, until I tour your new features, on the phone? Oh, and you also first want me to read a warning on the phone, and click a button to confirm that I’m not driving! Are you crazy? The primary use case for this app is going to be invoking it WHILE DRIVING! Don’t force users to their phones, to make the app work. And certainly don’t do such, simply because you updated the app and want to show me some new bells and whistles. (Like most iPhone users, I have my apps set to automatically update. It’s a mistake for you to assume that you are presenting this info at the time a user is manually updating it.) 8. Increase prominence of traffic markings The primary use cases for me, personally, is just using the map—without routing—to view local traffic when I already know how to get where I’m going, in order to decide for myself which route would be best. The traffic markings on the 620 are considerably more prominent than in this app, in CarPlay mode. It would be helpful to make the markings more prominent/thicker. 9. Add route bar I’m sure you must already know this one, since it’s an obvious absence in CarPlay mode. 10. Split-screen 3D view on turns The temporary split screen 3D view when a turn/action is upcoming, and one is in 2D view on the 620 is a nice feature. You should make it available in the app, also. --- I apologize for getting a little worked up with some of the comments, but some of the choices, (lack of) priorities, and oversights are a but dumbfounding. Anyway, I would love to give you folks $12.99/year for this app (and update this review 5 stars!). Please fix the above items to make the app worth paying for (I'm sure for many others also, beside myself).

title: May make sense in places with poor cell coverage?
body: My main motivation for using this app was to see if I could reduce my data usage while still having traffic data on my commute. Unfortunately, it uses about twice the data that Waze does driving the same route. Beyond that the experience is a lot like using a standalone GPS device from 2003–there are computer-generated voices that are very unnatural compared to current-day Siri/Google Assistant/Alexa. The maps are functional though unappealing with garish colors. I also found at times the app would place me on an overpass or ramp that other apps don’t seem to have an issue with. I do appreciate the lane guidance function (which most apps also have) and I like the route bar though that isn’t currently available with CarPlay.

title: Wrong Driving Speeds
body: I don’t get how Waze, Apple & Google Maps can calculate driving speeds correctly, but TomTom & Sygic both cannot calculate your actual speeds and think you’re speeding everywhere you go. The biggest issue I’ve been having is both it shows I’m speeding when I’m not....i drive 20 in a 25 zone, I’ speeding. I drive 65 in a. 75 zone, it’s lit up red like I’m speeding. Is there a way to turn off the visual notifications for speeding since your app cannot actually calculate speeds correctly? Also in my home are some of the speed limits are wrong. Shows 20mph speed zones when it’s 25. Or I’ve even see it show 30mph in a 45mph zone. Also, whose idea was it to not allow addresses/POI to be searched from the CarPlay? You can do all that from within the app and start your navigation and it picks up on the CarPlay. It’s more convenient to plug in your device, set down your phone and use the larger screen to input your trip. It would be nice to see the paid for big name maps be more reliable than the freebies, but I’m starting to see this as a waste of money until this map can be updated correctly. I got this for offline maps, but I’m not looking for incorrect offline maps either...

title: UPDATED: Only looks like it accesses Photos without permission
body: UPDATED REVIEW This is a much better response from the developer. And that’s appreciated. The original reply was incomprehensibly inadequate. I watched the entire Apple video linked below by the developer. To summarize, Apple introduced a new feature in WWDC 2020 called PHPicker that allows developers to access photos without ever having to prompt permission from the user or without actual access to the user’s Photo Library. PHPicker allows the same level of privacy (maybe more) as older methods, even though it appears like it doesn’t. While the photos “look” like they’re available inside the app, that’s just an illusion, as it only allows access to photos actually selected by the user from the picker. So … that explain everything and addresses my concern. A simple note from Apple inside the pop-up stating something to that extent would be VERY useful, so that users don’t get alarmed every time they see their entire photo library pop up inside apps (no doubt many developers are using this feature now) without ever having given permission. I’ve changed my review from 1 to 4 stars based on this response. I genuinely feel this is the best navigation app in the store — from features, to design, to functionality. I wish maps didn’t require downloading but that’s a small beef. ——- OLD REVIEW This app accesses your Photos without even asking for permission. Doesn’t even show up in Settings > Privacy as having asked! There’s a section in the app called Drive to Photos (Menu > Search > Favorites > Photos) where all of your Photos show up INSIDE the app without user permission. Apple does an excellent job of keeping this type of stuff in check, but this appears to have gotten past Apple reviewers. TomTom is clearly violating this policy. The Developer responded to my concern with this bafflingly useless comment: “you must have found the photos in some of the app files”. Wow. What does that even mean? Of course, I found it in the “app files”. My ENTIRE photo library! The point is I NEVER gave the app permission for even a single picture to be found in the “app files”. Nor did the app even ASK for permission. This must be reported to Apple by everyone who cares about privacy and security. I’m actively pursuing it with Apple, because, afaic, it’s a blatant violation of their policy and the developer clearly has no interest in addressing it (at best), or is being deceptive about it (at worst). It is impossible to contact a human at TomTom, chat or otherwise, so that has proven to be a useless route.

title: gets me there..
body: i’ve tried almost all map apps, from apple to google, and some that most have never heard of, and Tomtom is the only one that has an efficient mapping system ALONG WITH (and this is important for me) an audible warning of speed and red light cameras. Almost everyone offers speed camera alerts VISUALLY on the map but I find it EXTREMELY handy that tomtom is the only one that actually offers audible alerts so that I can be prepared for one way before I recognize I’m coming up on it on my own. If my next turn isn’t for 3 miles I’m not checking my carplay every 200 feet for visual alerts... i’m cruising for about a mile and a half before i look down again, so if a camera happens to pop up on the map that i’m unaware of, I get 3 pings in my stereo and a voice alerting me of said camera... THE BEST CAMERA SYSTEM OUT THERE RIGHT NOW.. the app itself has its kinks every now and then as I’ve seen with them all but overall a true 5/5 try not to change much in terms of functionality and I’ll be subscribing when my free trial is up.

title: Great nav app
body: I have owned every, yes every nav app in the Apple store. This app has reached the point where it outclasses them all. Several other apps rely on TomTom for their traffic data. Most all apps, except for Waze, actually consider and use carpool lanes correctly. And this app, like Waze, tracks traffic data in carpool lanes independent from normal traffic lanes. Most car nav apps don’t even recognize carpool lanes (Apple and Google). Other apps have carpool lanes as an option but they don’t have accurate maps or ever use carpool lanes. The large buttons on the app make adjustments easy. The map has really well thought out colors along with auto switching to night. You can option to route automatically around traffic or have the app advise you of faster routes and you can decide. The traffic is about as accurate as I’ve ever found. I travel through Los Angeles and Orange Counties. The new lane guidance is the best I’ve ever seen. iCloud syncing is a nice feature. My suggestions to developers would be Apple Watch integration, trip tracking, and weather routing.

title: Still the Best Navigation App
body: So glad to see TomTom back on CarPlay now. My car navigation system upgraded to CarPlay over 8 months ago. I’ve always preferred TomTom, and this was confirmed because I’ve been living with Apple and Google Maps only because they’re the only CarPlay navigation systems I had. I wondered if I’d just get used to it and adopt native Apple Maps after such a long wait for TomTom CarPlay. I never did and am glad to be able to use TomTom again. TomTom is much better than the free alternatives, and the older app it replaced—I’ve seen it provide better routes than before, its alternate route interface is better, its traffic interface is much better, and both worldwide and regional map downloads help with memory footprint. I expect TomTom Go will continue to be improved with regular updates. My own requests are Siri integration, and Contacts integration within CarPlay—the two features of Apple Maps I used the most.

title: New TomTom better than the other navigation apps
body: Version 2 now supports CarPlay. For a couple of months, I have been using four other popular navigation apps. They each have pluses and missing features. For a week now, I have been using TomTom v2. Although the TomTom CarPlay is still in need of more development, it couples with the iPhone app to give full features that anyone would need. The other apps dumb down the iPhone app when connected to carPlay; TomTom allows the full feature set on the iPhone when connected to CarPlay. Hopefully with the new CarPlay in iOS 13, TomTom has the chance to incorporate its more sophisticated features on the CarPlay display. For now, TomTom will be my go to navigation app whether I am in my car with CarPlay or my in my car that CarPlay is never going to be available. The base iPhone app does have improvements over the version 1 app.

I initially chose TomTom over others because the app could guide me offline if I didn't have data - possible when driving. I've owned a TomTom navigation app since you used to have to buy the app (more than $40.00) plus a traffic subscription. TomTom switched to the free "Go" app and honored their commitment to us by giving us three years of free traffic (worth $60.00).
